James Madison insisted that our bicameral Congress is America’s “preeminent” branch of government—not the president, whose primary job is to “take Care” to faithfully execute our laws, and the Supreme Court whose job is to say what the law is.  I wrote in @thenation about the nonsense of “co-equal” branches and how we must advance the voting rights of the people and restore decisive power to our elected representatives in Congress. thenation.com/article/societ…

Link



We Must Restore Congress

posts.text: On this day in 1964, America moved toward realizing the promise of equal justice under law. Passage of the Civil Rights Act after Freedom Summer and the deaths of Schwerner, Chaney and Goodman, reminds us that every hard-won right has come through courage, collective action and a passionate belief in democratic change. Today, it’s our turn to fight back in the face of rampant authoritarianism to guard the rights and liberties of our people.

posts.text: President Trump’s quest to destroy birthright citizenship has failed. The president’s executive order was a direct and blatant violation of the first sentence of the Fourteenth Amendment, as numerous district and appeals court judges ruled. Today, a narrow majority of the Supreme Court, including one justice nominated by Trump himself (Barrett), rejected the President’s blood-and-soil attempt to deny a huge number of children born in America their equal constitutional birthright.
